corrected_proposal.description_short: Unverified claim: federal agencies restricted benefits for same-sex spouses in February 2025.

corrected_proposal.description_long: The supplied record alleges that the Trump administration changed federal benefits rules in February 2025 to disadvantage same-sex married couples, naming Social Security survivor benefits, federal employee health coverage, and spousal immigration rights. The packet includes no directive or contemporaneous report establishing those changes. It also says the marriages themselves remained legally recognized; no sourced material here establishes a change to that status. Social Security Administration guidance dated February 7, 2025 treats same-sex and opposite-sex marriages alike for two specific Medicare procedures: special enrollment eligibility and rollback of a premium surcharge. Those limited procedures do not determine whether survivor benefits, federal employee coverage, or immigration rules changed. The broad policy allegation therefore remains unverified, and the supplied materials do not establish which agency acted, what rule changed, when it took effect, or who was affected. No measured impact or outcome is documented.

Same-sex marriages are treated the same as opposite-sex marriages for purposes of the premium surcharge rollback. The sex of the married individuals, domicile and date of marriage are not factors in determining eligibility for the premium surcharge rollback.

corrected_proposal.title: Trump Revoked EO 11246 and Changed Federal Contractor DEI Rules
corrected_proposal.description_short: A Jan. 21 order revoked EO 11246, set a 90-day transition, and limited contractor certification to DEI programs that violate federal law.
corrected_proposal.description_medium: On January 21, 2025, President Donald Trump revoked Executive Order 11246, which governed equal-employment requirements for federal contractors. The order allowed contractors to continue under the January 20 regulatory scheme for 90 days during the transition. It directed agencies to require certification that a contractor does not operate DEI programs that violate federal anti-discrimination law; it did not require contractors to eliminate every DEI program.
corrected_proposal.description_long: On January 21, 2025, President Donald Trump signed the order “Ending Illegal Discrimination and Restoring Merit-Based Opportunity.” Section 3 revoked Executive Order 11246, the federal contractor equal-employment order, and allowed contractors to continue complying with the regulatory scheme in effect on January 20 for 90 days. It directed the Labor Department's Office of Federal Contract Compliance Programs to stop holding contractors responsible for affirmative action and related practices described in the order. The order also required agencies to add contract terms concerning compliance with federal anti-discrimination laws and certification that a contractor does not operate DEI programs that violate those laws. That language is narrower than the frozen entry's claim that all contractor DEI requirements ended immediately or that contractors had to eliminate all DEI programs. The order took effect as an executive directive on January 21, but the 90-day transition means the change was staged. This record describes the order and its text; it makes no claim about court outcomes or documented injuries to a specific contractor, employee, or protected group.
